transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Lately I keep thinking my family might be better off without me, and those thoughts are starting to scare me. I've never felt this way before, and I knew I needed to get some help.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this low, hopeless, or disconnected from things you enjoy at any point in your life before this current episode?

Yes, looking back, these swings between crashing into deep, heavy lows and then feeling overly revved up with big plans have been coming and going for several years. This current stretch since my business contracts fell through is definitely the worst it has ever been, though.

During those periods when you felt 'overly revved up,' did you ever experience things like hearing voices, seeing things others couldn't, or feeling like you had special powers or hidden messages meant only for you?

No, I've never heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or believed I had supernatural powers. But during those high times, I did have this intense, almost unrealistic confidence, like I had a special gift for woodworking that nobody else in town could match.

During these current periods of feeling low, have you experienced any physical symptoms like significant changes in your sleep or appetite, or have you noticed a complete loss of interest in all activities you usually enjoy?

I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like designing furniture or going salsa dancing with my wife, and now I just end up sitting on the couch. Even though I'm sleeping, I wake up feeling completely drained of energy, though my appetite has stayed pretty much the same.
During these current periods of feeling low, have you experienced any feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or slowed-down movements that others have noticed?

Yes, I constantly beat myself up over my business decisions, feeling like a complete failure as a provider who ruined my family's life. My wife has also pointed out that I move like I’m walking through mud, and it takes me a long time just to pick up my tools or answer a simple question.

During those periods when you felt 'overly revved up,' did you ever experience any other symptoms like racing thoughts, needing very little sleep, or engaging in risky behaviors like spending excessive amounts of money?

Yes, I definitely needed very little sleep during those times, often staying up until 2 or 3 in the morning working in the shop and not feeling tired at all the next day. I don't recall having racing thoughts or doing any risky spending, but I talked nonstop and my mind was so buzzing with big plans that I was easily distracted.

During those periods when you felt 'overly revved up,' did you ever feel that your thoughts were so intense or special that they were being broadcast to others, or that someone was trying to interfere with your mind?

No, I never felt like my thoughts were being broadcasted or that anyone was trying to interfere with my mind. Even though my thoughts were fast and I felt very confident back then, it never went that far.

During those periods of feeling 'overly revved up,' did you ever feel like you were so powerful or important that you were on a special mission, or did anyone ever express concern that your behavior during those times was so extreme it required hospitalization?

No, I never felt like I was on a special mission, and my behavior was never extreme enough to warrant going to a hospital. While I did feel highly confident—believing I had a special gift to make my shop famous and getting very snappy when my family questioned me—it never reached that level of needing medical care.
During this current period of feeling low, have you experienced any thoughts of ending your life or made any plans to carry them out?

I have, and it really frightens me. On my worst nights, I've pictured hanging myself in the workshop or driving off the cliff road. What scares me the most is how calm and reasonable those thoughts actually start to sound in those moments.
